content.title: Submit a just-over-limit order for approval when tax and delivery push the total above $25,000
content.intent: Prove that approval routing uses the final order total including tax and delivery, shows the over-limit review state, and creates a pending approval request when the buyer submits.
content.technique_notes: Applied eqp to separate <=$25,000 direct placement from >$25,000 approval routing. Applied bva using the just-over-limit representative 25001 from expand_bva({min:25000,max:25000}). Applied state_flow because the promise spans order review to approval submission. Applied auth because Procurement Manager approval is the gate. covering_array used requested strength 3 from money+auth risk and degraded to strength 1 because threshold_case was the only grounded input. Budget ceiling 2 kept this path.

content.title: Keep an order totaling exactly $25,000 on direct placement without approval
content.intent: Prove that the spending rule is strict: an order at exactly $25,000 does not require approval and does not enter the approval path.
content.technique_notes: Applied bva using the threshold representative 25000 from expand_bva({min:25000,max:25000}). Applied negative to prove absence of approval routing at the boundary. Applied eqp because orders at or below $25,000 share the direct-placement outcome class. covering_array used requested strength 3 from money+auth risk and degraded to strength 1 because threshold_case was the only grounded input. Budget ceiling 2 kept this path because an off-by-one defect would misroute orders.

judgements.rationale: [applicability] Applied equivalence partitioning, boundary analysis, auth, and state/flow because the source defines a strict monetary threshold, an approval gate, and a submit transition. Did not mint separate a11y, perf, i18n, concurrency, pagination, or persistence scenarios because the source text for this use case made no explicit promise in those families.

[applicability] Applied boundary analysis and a negative absence-of-approval check because the source distinguishes 'exceeds $25,000' from 'at or below $25,000'. Did not add a separate under-limit scenario because 24999 and 25000 share the same direct-placement outcome class and the stricter threshold point carried the highest defect-finding value under the budget.
